panels.title: Gateway scrapes healthy

defaults.noValue: no gateway target is configured

panels.description: One only when every configured gateway target answered its latest scrape. The minimum exposes a failed A/B target instead of letting a healthy peer hide it.

panels.title: Requests per minute

defaults.noValue: the gateway was not scraped

panels.description: Chat requests per minute each gateway handled over the last fifteen minutes, every outcome counted.

panels.title: Requests in flight

defaults.noValue: no gateway has an active DevShard

panels.description: Requests each active gateway is serving right now. Gateways without an active DevShard are hidden.

panels.title: Success rate (15m)

defaults.noValue: no gateway received a request in fifteen minutes

panels.description: Share of requests each gateway answered successfully over fifteen minutes. Empty for a gateway with no requests.

panels.title: Capacity available

defaults.noValue: no gateway has an active DevShard

panels.description: Share of baseline capacity each active gateway can route to. Gateways without an active DevShard are hidden.

panels.title: Participant-budget rejections (7d)

defaults.noValue: no rejection counter was scraped

panels.description: Attempts refused by a per-participant budget. The build exports no gateway-wide rejection counter, so this is the participant-scoped one.

panels.title: Request rate by gateway and outcome

defaults.noValue: the gateway has counted no request yet

panels.description: Requests per second by gateway and user-visible outcome. Separate A/B series prevent an active gateway from hiding an idle or failed peer.

panels.title: Attempts by gateway and role

defaults.noValue: the gateway has started no attempt yet

panels.description: Attempts each gateway started per second over five minutes. Primary attempts follow requests one to one; secondary ones are extra attempts the gateway starts on another executor.

panels.title: Secondary attempts by reason

defaults.noValue: no gateway started a secondary attempt in five minutes

panels.description: Why each gateway started a second attempt: a speedup or A/B sample it planned, or a primary that looked slow, suspicious or failed. Gateways that start none are not drawn.

panels.title: Failed requests (15m)

defaults.noValue: no request failed in fifteen minutes

panels.description: Requests the gateways failed in fifteen minutes, by reason.

panels.title: Requests by gateway, model and outcome

defaults.noValue: the gateway has counted no request yet

panels.description: Every request the gateway has counted, by A/B gateway, model, user-visible outcome and bounded reason.

panels.title: Current model executors

defaults.noValue: the gateway tracks no executor

panels.description: Rows appear once a participant is registered with the gateway for a model. An empty table means no executor is tracked at all, not that every executor is idle.

panels.title: First content latency p50

defaults.noValue: no first-content histogram was scraped

panels.description: Time from gateway send to first content, over a six-hour window. The window is wide because the gateway observes only a few attempts an hour; a narrower one leaves the line undefined between bursts.

panels.title: First content latency p95

defaults.noValue: no first-content histogram was scraped

panels.description: Time from gateway send to first content, over a six-hour window. The window is wide because the gateway observes only a few attempts an hour; a narrower one leaves the line undefined between bursts.

panels.title: Attempt latency by executor

defaults.noValue: no attempt duration histogram was scraped

panels.description: Mean attempt duration per executor over a six-hour window. Dividing the totals instead would average every attempt since the gateway started.

panels.title: Executor wins

defaults.noValue: no executor has won a request yet

panels.description: Requests each executor won for a model. A win is a routed completion the user received.

panels.title: Executor failures

defaults.noValue: no attempt has failed yet, or the gateway was not scraped

panels.description: Attempts that failed per executor, model and reason.

panels.title: Quarantine state

defaults.noValue: the gateway tracks no participant

panels.description: Quarantine state exists per participant and model. An empty table means the gateway is tracking no participant, which is not the same as every participant being healthy.

panels.title: Effective and baseline weight

defaults.noValue: the gateway published no capacity weight

panels.description: Both weights carry the same labels, so joining them with or showed only the effective one.

panels.title: Escrow effective weight

defaults.noValue: no escrow is active

panels.description: Summed across escrows: the identifier churns with every escrow, so one line per escrow filled the legend with hundreds of rows.

panels.title: Blocked participants

defaults.noValue: no escrow is active

panels.description: A zero is a measured escrow blocking nobody. Empty means no escrow is active.

panels.title: Participant-budget rejection rate

defaults.noValue: no rejection counter was scraped

panels.description: The build exports no gateway-wide rejection counter, so the three-way or chain only ever showed the participant-scoped one.

panels.title: Hidden participant failures

defaults.noValue: no request has hidden a failure yet, or the gateway was not scraped

panels.description: Requests the user received although an executor failed behind them. A zero is a measured clean path.

panels.title: Oldest gateway scrape age

defaults.noValue: a gateway target is down or has no successful scrape

panels.description: Seconds since the oldest successful A/B gateway scrape. It is empty when any target is down, rather than letting a newer peer hide a failed scrape.

panels.title: Executors tracked

defaults.noValue: the gateway is not scraped

panels.description: Executors the gateway is currently tracking, as the gateway itself reports.

panels.title: Models observed

defaults.noValue: the gateway has counted no request yet

panels.description: Models the gateway has counted a request for.

panels.title: Transport errors (7d)

defaults.noValue: no transport error counter was scraped

panels.description: Executor transport failures in the window.

panels.title: Telegram exporter age

defaults.noValue: the bot exporter is not scraped

panels.description: Seconds since Prometheus last scraped the bot exporter. The whole Telegram row below is gated on that scrape.

panels.title: Active gateways

defaults.noValue: no gateway reports an active DevShard

panels.description: Gateways that report an active DevShard in their status.

defaults.noValue: the bot exporter is not scraped

panels.description: Read from the bot exporter and shown only while Prometheus scrapes it. The metrics file the bot also writes changes only on activity, so its age is not a liveness signal.

panels.title: Time since last successful bot inference

defaults.noValue: the bot exporter is not scraped

panels.description: Zero would have read as a success just now, the most reassuring possible value for a consumer that never answered. Empty now means the bot exporter is not scraped.

panels.description: Read from the bot exporter and shown only while Prometheus scrapes it. The metrics file the bot also writes changes only on activity, so its age is not a liveness signal.

panels.title: Consumer process

defaults.noValue: the bot exporter is not scraped; the state of the bot is unknown

panels.description: Running only while Prometheus scrapes the bot exporter. A stopped bot drops out of the scrape instead of keeping its last state.

panels.title: Nonces per inference

defaults.noValue: no gateway reports nonce accounting

panels.description: Nonces each gateway assigned in its current escrow per nonce that produced a used result. Both counts restart when the gateway rotates its escrow.

panels.title: Burned nonces

defaults.noValue: no gateway reports nonce accounting

panels.description: Nonces committed in the current escrow and never sent to a host: paid, with no inference behind them. The count restarts at rotation.

panels.title: Cost per nonce

defaults.noValue: no escrow has been settled yet

panels.description: Host payout plus nonce fees divided by the nonces paid, over every settled escrow on the chain.

panels.title: Cost per inference

defaults.noValue: no escrow has been settled yet, or no gateway reports nonce accounting

targets.expr: (sum by (gateway) (devshard_accounting_assigned_nonces) / sum by (gateway) (devshard_accounting_disposition{disposition="finished_used"})) * on() group_left() ((sum(gdc_chain_escrow_payout_ngonka) + sum(gdc_chain_escrow_fees_ngonka)) / sum(gdc_chain_escrow_settled_nonces))

panels.description: Cost per nonce times the nonces each gateway spends per used result. An estimate that follows the current escrow of each gateway.

panels.title: Escrows created (24h)

defaults.noValue: the chain poller reports no escrow creation

panels.description: Escrows each creator wallet opened in the last day, by block time.

panels.title: Unsettled escrows

defaults.noValue: the chain poller reports no escrow creation

panels.description: Escrows created and not settled. Their amount stays held until settlement.

panels.title: Escrows created per hour

defaults.noValue: the chain poller reports no escrow creation

panels.description: Escrows each creator wallet opened in the past hour, by block time. A gateway opens a new escrow when the current one nears max_nonce or its epoch ends.

panels.title: Held in unsettled escrows

defaults.noValue: the chain poller reports no unsettled escrow

panels.description: Amount of the escrows not yet settled per creator wallet, in ngonka.

panels.title: Creator wallet balance

defaults.noValue: the chain poller reports no creator wallet

panels.description: ngonka left in each wallet allowed to create escrows. Each new escrow takes its amount from here.

panels.title: Heap in use

defaults.noValue: no gateway with an active DevShard exports this metric

panels.description: Go heap spans in use by each gateway. Under steady load it should level off; a line that keeps rising points at retained state.

panels.title: Heap allocated

defaults.noValue: no gateway with an active DevShard exports this metric

panels.description: Bytes of live heap objects; it drops after each garbage collection.

panels.title: Resident memory

defaults.noValue: no gateway with an active DevShard exports this metric

panels.description: Memory the gateway process holds in RAM, as the operating system sees it.

panels.title: Heap held, not returned

defaults.noValue: no gateway with an active DevShard exports this metric

panels.description: Idle heap the Go runtime keeps instead of returning it to the system: room for the next burst, not leaked memory.

panels.title: Heap objects

defaults.noValue: no gateway with an active DevShard exports this metric

panels.description: Live objects on the heap. Growth with a flat request rate means objects are kept between requests.

panels.title: Goroutines

defaults.noValue: no gateway with an active DevShard exports this metric

panels.description: Goroutines per gateway. A count that keeps rising with steady load is a leak candidate.

panels.title: Garbage collections per minute

defaults.noValue: no gateway with an active DevShard exports this metric

panels.description: How often each gateway runs garbage collection.

panels.title: Requests in flight

defaults.noValue: no gateway with an active DevShard exports this metric

panels.description: Requests each gateway is serving, to compare with its memory.

panels.title: Requests per second

defaults.noValue: no gateway with an active DevShard exports this metric

panels.description: Requests each gateway handled per second over five minutes.

panels.title: Response cache

defaults.noValue: no gateway with an active DevShard exports this metric

targets.expr: sum by (gateway, result) (rate(devshard_gateway_chat_cache_total[5m])) and on (gateway) (max by (gateway) (gdc_chain_gateway_working) == 1)

panels.description: Cache outcomes per second: hit is served from cache, stored is a new entry, skipped_* is not cached. Only v6 gateways export these outcomes, and no gateway exports a cache size.

panels.title: Live inferences

defaults.noValue: no DevShard host metrics are scraped

panels.description: Inferences each Host keeps in memory across its DevShard sessions. A count that keeps rising under steady load is retained state.

panels.title: Sessions

defaults.noValue: no DevShard host metrics are scraped

panels.description: DevShard sessions open on each Host, one per escrow it serves.

panels.title: Mempool entries

defaults.noValue: no DevShard host metrics are scraped

panels.description: Entries waiting in the DevShard mempool of each Host.

panels.title: ML node call failures

defaults.noValue: no DevShard host metrics are scraped

panels.description: Calls from the Host to its ML nodes that did not succeed, per second. acquire_err means the Host could not acquire an ML node for the call.

panels.title: ML node call p95

defaults.noValue: no DevShard host metrics are scraped

panels.description: 95th percentile duration of a call from the Host to its ML node over five minutes.

panels.title: Request errors

defaults.noValue: no DevShard host metrics are scraped

panels.description: Errors per second of each DevShard operation on the Host.

panels.title: Interrupted executions

defaults.noValue: no DevShard host metrics are scraped

panels.description: Executions that ended without a finish, per second and reason.

panels.title: Validation queue

defaults.noValue: no DevShard host metrics are scraped

panels.description: Validations queued and owed by each Host across its escrows. Owed validations that keep growing are work the Host falls behind on.

panels.title: Postgres pool saturated

defaults.noValue: no DevShard host metrics are scraped

panels.description: One while the payload Postgres pool of the Host has no free connection.
